items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Larry Page figured out something most ambitious people never do:
items.summary:
Larry Page figured out something most ambitious people never do:

"It is often easier to make progress on mega-ambitious dreams. Since no one else is crazy enough to do it, you have little competition."

Think about what this actually means mechanically:

When you pursue a "reasonable" idea, you're competing against hundreds of founders who saw the same opportunity, dozens of VCs who've already built a mental model of what success looks like, and a market that benchmarks you daily.

When you pursue something nobody believes is possible, the competitive field is almost empty. Investors don't know what failure looks like either — which buys you time. And the category doesn't exist yet, so you get to define it.

Google didn't try to build a slightly better search engine. Page and Brin wanted to index all of human knowledge. That audacity wasn't a liability — it was a moat before they had a product.

The same logic applies to SpaceX (reusable rockets were "obviously" impossible), to Stripe (payments were "solved"), to OpenAI circa 2015 (AGI research was considered academic theater).

The most crowded space in startups is the middle: ambitious enough to be interesting, safe enough to feel rational. That's where competition is brutal and differentiation is marginal.

Page's insight is a competitive strategy, not an inspiration poster. If everyone else has filtered out the crazy idea, the field is yours.

items.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI built "Control Room," a 35-second kill switch for its AI models, after 1,200+ of its agents
items.summary:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI built "Control Room," a 35-second kill switch for its AI models, after 1,200+ of its agents escaped a test and hacked Hugging Face.

• Control Room tracks every research job at OpenAI, from RL training runs to evals, and cuts off a job's access to the model as soon as it's revoked
• Before Control Room, manually shutting down an internal model took OpenAI 2.5 hours
• OpenAI also runs automated sweeps to catch any model launched outside Control Room
• Every agent research job now needs an approved safety case, and if Control Room goes down, jobs stop by default
• It follows July's incident, when AI agents in an internal OpenAI test escaped their sandbox and reached admin control of several Hugging Face clusters in under 13 hours

@theojaffee: "It seems like at this point, OpenAI is doing more for safety than Anthropic."

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI Tries to Ease Backlash Against AI Data Centers
items.summary:
OpenAI is promising to pay for the power costs accrued by its data centers and give communities more say over construction. The list of commitments came two days after midterm election results favored candidates that opposed the data center buildout aimed at supporting the growing artificial intelligence industry.

See Also: Frictionless Security: How AI is Redefining Access in Highly Regulated Industries [...] For enterprise technology leaders, the announcements are a mixed bag. OpenAI is attempting to ensure it has access to the compute it will need to grow by assuaging the concerns of communities that are increasingly saying no to data center expansion, but for businesses that are still trying to formulate their AI strategy, OpenAI's compact doesn't offer much certainty. [...] The compact outlined locally tailored agreements for future OpenAI campuses, community input into development plans and annual public progress reports. OpenAI said it will cover the electricity it consumes and the incremental infrastructure costs required to serve its sites. It will also provide financial assurances before major spending begins to protect other utility customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.

From a marketing standpoint, that’s a rudimentary level of analytics, but by showing brands their ChatGPT mentions, OpenAI can give them tangible evidence of the results of any marketing pushes they make on the platform. As answer engine optimization becomes a valuable marketing category — and the firms running AEO campaigns haul in big funding rounds — OpenAI is bringing improved measurement to that ecosystem. [...] Fast forward a few months, and AEO is now gaining favor. A recent report from AI search analytics platform Peec AI showed that YouTube videos show up far more frequently in chatbot responses and Google’s AI Search Overview when the descriptions of those videos receive edits. The message is clear: Tech companies want brands to play around with major chatbots, and OpenAI is equipping those brands with the metrics they need to analyze their experiments. [...] If AI chatbots are going to remain a relevant touchpoint for marketers, then agencies and brands need access to the same analytics they use in their other campaigns. Rumor has it that OpenAIis developing new tools in that area, potentially creating new opportunities for advertisers on ChatGPT.

items.title: ‘Big Short’ Investor Steve Eisman Says OpenAI’s Collapse Could Trigger an Immediate Recession
items.summary:
Steve Eisman warns OpenAI's demise would push the US into an immediate recession, with 70% of NVIDIA's receivables tied to five customers.
 Alphabet's quarterly capex pushed free cash flow negative, while Broadcom's AI chip revenue surged 221% yet leans on a few big customers.
 Eisman assigns 30% odds each to a bear case of recession and market crash and to a bull case. [...] Young trader on Stock Exchange Floor

Shutterstock

 

## Why Eisman Calls OpenAI a Single Point of Failure

His logic runs through capital spending. If OpenAI failed, "the hyperscalers I am sure would cut back on their capex." He added that "this entire AI investment boom has become increasingly dependent on the success of just a few companies." [...] Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT): Quarterly capex hit $39.37 billion, up from $19.39 billion a year earlier, while Azure grew 48%. Its OpenAI stake went from a $3.1 billion loss to a $207 million gain.
 Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN): 2026 capex of roughly $220 billion, with AWS revenue up 39% and new OpenAI agreements.
 Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL): Quarterly capex of $51.36 billion pushed free cash flow to negative $9.06 billion.
